cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Tell Me Why
cards.instruction: Get someone to reveal the motive behind a choice by offering small pieces of your own truth as bait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're circling the station. You used to dodge a question this way when I coached your interviews. I avoid my old office too; why this route?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My former boss catches this train.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, a straight answer. I told mine I'd become a novelist. What did you tell yours?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That I had a better offer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I carry a blank notebook past mine. Nothing to show him. You remember how I made you give an example after a claim? What offer are you avoiding showing yours?

reason: Give the familiar training relationship a concrete role in the exact pursuit. Keep D137 planned-design claims distinct from D140 improvement claims, and make truth bait or procedure borrowing depend on actual B replies.
